_meta.description: Rolling registry of recent post generation characteristics. Used to inject differentiation context into future generation prompts, preventing hook repetition, title cadence cloning, and emotional arc duplication. Capped at 30 recent entries per category.
_meta.usage: Read by scripts/lib/generation-memory.js before generation. Written after each successful post creation. Pass result to generate-post.js as differentiation context.

recentHooks.hook: Here is a strange test. Try to sit in a chair with nothing in your hands for two minutes. No phone, no music, no plan. Most people cannot do it. Their hand reaches for the phone before their brain eve
Here is a strange thing about tires spinning in mud. The engine is roaring. The wheels are moving fast. You are pouring in effort. And you are going absolutely nowhere.
You catch your reflection in a store window and it takes half a second to recognize the person walking toward you.

Wired and tired at the same time. That is the phrase people reach for when they finally describe it out loud. Your body is buzzing like it drank six coffees, but you can barely lift your arm off the c
Here's a question nobody wants answered honestly: why does the thing you swore off last night feel almost mandatory tonight?

There's a specific kind of quiet that shows up around 9pm when the dishes are done and the day was fine and you should feel content, but instead you feel like a stranger renting your own life.
Your brain feels like a radio caught between two stations. Static. Fragments. Nothing lands.
You didn't do anything hard today. You barely left the couch. So why do you feel like you got hit by a truck?
Here is a question worth sitting with before you read another word: when was the last time you kept a promise to yourself that nobody else knew about?
You already know the answer to the thing you keep asking everyone about. You just can't hear it under all the static.

What if the reason you can't focus, can't finish, and can't sit still has nothing to do with willpower?
It's 12:40am. You told yourself 11:00 was the cutoff. You are still awake, thumb moving, watching a stranger reorganize a pantry you will never see again.
Picture the small notebook by your bed. On page one, in your own handwriting, is a promise you made three weeks ago. You have not looked at it since. And some part of you already knows why.

You can name three trending topics, five people's hot takes, and a podcast host's opinion on a decision that is actually yours to make. But when someone asks what you want, the answer comes back fuzzy

A follower reads your caption and thinks, "Something's off." They cannot name it. But the warmth is gone. The little weird word choices you always used, gone. It reads clean and dead, like a hotel lob

You read the same sentence four times and still have no idea what it said. Your eyes moved. The words went in. Nothing landed.
